observation.visible_scene: A fire burning against a black night sky. A bright yellow-white flame mass stays anchored in the lower-left to lower-center of the frame throughout the excerpt, while a taller, dimmer orange plume rises above it and repeatedly changes shape. Small glowing embers/sparks are scattered in the dark background. The overall framing of the bright base appears fixed, so the dominant motion is the flame's own deformation rather than scene translation.
visible_changes: The rising plume cycles between a rightward-curving hook/loop (frames 1-3, 31-36) and a more vertical column with a curling top (frames 19-26, 37-41).
In several frames (4-5, 8-9, 16-18, 27) the upper part of the plume breaks into detached wisps and puffs that drift upward and fade, while the bright base remains connected below.
The bright core at the bottom expands and contracts and shifts its outline continuously (e.g., broad rounded bulge in frames 28-30 vs. narrower column in frames 21-26).
The plume's tip position moves relative to the fixed base: upper-right early on, upper-center mid-segment, then back to a rightward hook near the end.
The hook/loop shape forms, loosens into diffuse orange smoke, and re-forms multiple times without the base flame leaving its lower-left/center position.
outside_clip_unknowns: What material is burning and the ignition source are not visible.
Whether the fire's intensity is increasing, steady, or decreasing overall cannot be judged from this short crop.
The cause of the plume's curling (wind, fuel feed, or buoyancy) is not shown.
Events before t=0 and after t=2.669 s are outside the segment.
uncertain_details: Camera motion is not clearly evidenced; the dark background gives few reference points, so the base's apparent stability could include minor drift.
It is ambiguous whether the detached upper wisps are separate flame tongues or cooler smoke/embers.
The exact boundary between flame and smoke in the dimmer orange regions is uncertain.
